title: Introduce batch-cache constraint suggester and soft-quant rollback operator
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds tenant-facing constraint suggester for batch/cache defaults, a soft rollback flow for quantization profiles, and an offline econometrics simulator. Backwards-compatible: new features are opt-in via tenant policy flags.
description: Summary: This PR adds a tenant-level 'BatchCache Constraint Suggester' that recommends conservative batching and cache settings based on observed latency percentiles, token distributions, and unit-econ thresholds. It also introduces a soft-rollback operator for quantization profiles so the system can gracefully revert to a safer numeric format when quality regressions are detected. Motivation: customers consistently ask for automated, explainable defaults that reduce unit cost without risking visible regressions. Manual tinkering (per-tenant) is error-prone. This change ships an automated advisor plus a small simulation harness to validate economic impact before applying changes in production. What changed: 1) services/econ/suggester.py: new constraint engine implementing tenant policy inputs, SLO scoring, and a recommendation exporter. 2) tools/simulate/econ_sim.py: lightweight Monte Carlo-style offline simulator that estimates tokens saved, latency distribution shifts, and an expected cost delta. 3) runtime/quant/soft_rollback.py: orchestrates a canary for quant profile changes and a timed rollback if quality metrics cross thresholds. 4) infra/helm/values-cost.yaml: adds feature flags and default safe policies for Dedicated and Private deployments. 5) docs/recipes/tenant-optimizer.md: operational guide and examples for on-call and SRE teams. 6) tests/*: unit and integration tests covering suggester heuristics, simulation determinism, and rollback gating. Commits: ["init: add constraint suggester core and interfaces", "sim: add econ simulator and CLI dry-run", "runtime: soft quant rollback and health checks", "docs: tenant optimizer recipe and walkthrough", "tests: add synthetic traces and assertions"] CI: initial CI run had a lint failure in runtime/quant/soft_rollback.py (missing typed comment) which was fixed in the second commit; full test matrix passes on Linux and macOS, and the Dockerized integration job passed. Migration/Compatibility: all changes are guarded behind tenant policy flags (feature toggle) and default to disabled for older clusters. The Helm values add safe defaults to turn the feature on in new clusters. Rollout plan: staged canary on 10 tenants -> monitor unit-econ + subjective quality alerts -> 25% rollout -> full rollout. Checklist: - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration simulation coverage - [x] docs and runbook updated - [x] e2e smoke on staging - [x] security review (no secrets added) Related: ENG-1879 (tenant optimizer RFC), SUP-4123 (customer request: unpredictable inference costs). Links: RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1879/tenant-optimizer, support ticket: https://internal.redwood/support/SUP-4123

notes_for_ops: Feature is gated by helm value 'econ.constraint_suggester.enabled' and runtime flag 'ECON_SUGGESTER_ENABLE'. To enable soft rollback for quant profiles set 'runtime.quant.soft_rollback=true'. The staging rollout used an observability dashboard 'econ/tenant-optimizer' (dash id: ECO-019) and released to 10 canary tenants for 48h before scaling. If regressions appear, flip helm flag to false or revert the single 'soft rollback' controller in runtime.
